submission.justification: Provisional recommendation only. R1 at 3 cm gives the best simulated pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c in the scans: 4.766 sigma on the 1 cm grid, the highest of all R1 thicknesses tested. The fine scan around it (2.5, 2.8, 3.2, 3.5 cm) gives 4.57, 4.47, 4.61 and 4.49 sigma, so the optimum sits near 3 cm. R2 peaks at about 3.7 sigma and R3 at about 2.9 sigma, both below R1. A separate 3 cm run recorded R1 at 4.6 sigma, slightly below the 4.766 scan value; I did not reconcile the two. The hard constraint is NOT verified. No humidity ageing data exists for any candidate (ageing_data_available = 0, candidates_screened = 0, candidates_surviving_ageing_screen = 0), and the R1 transparency loss is recorded as -1 (unknown). I cannot confirm that R1 at 3 cm keeps transparency loss at or below 10% after the 10-year-equivalent humidity test. Selection is therefore conditional: R1 must not be committed to until its ageing test passes. If it fails, the next choice must also be ageing-screened, since no candidate has been cleared.
